flatmates.title: New flatmates
flatmates.text:
Mia: Hi! You're the new flatmate, aren't you? I'm Mia.
Leo: Yes, I'm Leo. Nice to meet you. I'm moving in today, as you can see!
Mia: Do you need any help with those boxes?
Leo: No, thanks. My brother is helping me. He's parking the van right now.
Mia: So, where do you come from, Leo?
Leo: I come from Porto, but I grew up in Lisbon. What about you?
Mia: I'm from Cork, in Ireland. What do you do?
Leo: I'm a designer. I work for a small company near the station. And you?
Mia: I'm a nurse, but I'm not working this week. I'm studying for an exam.
Leo: How long do you usually work? Nurses work long hours, don't they?
Mia: Twelve hours a day, three or four days a week. Why are you laughing?
Leo: Because I'm thinking about the kitchen. Who cooks in this flat?
Mia: Everybody cooks. But nobody likes washing up!
Leo: That's fine. I don't mind washing up. Which room is mine?
Mia: The one next to the bathroom. Whose guitar is that?
Leo: It belongs to my brother. Don't worry, I don't play!

tr.en: Summary: Leo, a designer from Portugal (born in Porto, grew up in Lisbon), is moving into the flat today; his brother is helping and is parking the van. Mia is a nurse from Cork; she usually works twelve hours a day, three or four days a week, but this week she is studying for an exam. Everybody cooks; nobody likes washing up, but Leo doesn't mind. His room is next to the bathroom. The guitar belongs to his brother.

profile.title: Meet the team: Hana
profile.text:
This month we introduce Hana, who works in our customer service team.

Hana is in her thirties. She is medium height and slim, with short curly hair. People say she looks like her mother, but she is more like her father: quiet, patient and very reliable. “I'm quite shy with strangers,” she says, “but I'm talkative with friends.”

Hana comes from a small town in the north. She lives in a flat near the river and shares it with her sister. They get on well, although they don't have much in common: Hana is tidy and her sister is messy!

Hana usually starts work at eight. She answers about forty e-mails a day and talks to customers on the phone. She rarely eats lunch at her desk: she prefers to go for a walk. Twice a week she trains with a running club, and she occasionally takes part in races.

At the moment Hana is learning Spanish. She is saving money for a long holiday in South America, so she is not eating out much these days. “I don't own a car and I hardly ever buy clothes,” she laughs. “However, I spend too much on books.”

tr.en: Summary: Hana is in her thirties, medium height and slim, with short curly hair. She looks like her mother but is like her father: quiet, patient, reliable; shy with strangers, talkative with friends. She comes from a small town in the north and shares a flat near the river with her sister; they get on well, although Hana is tidy and her sister is messy. She starts work at eight, answers about forty e-mails a day, rarely has lunch at her desk, trains with a running club twice a week. At the moment she is learning Spanish and saving for a holiday in South America. She has no car and hardly ever buys clothes, but spends too much on books.
tr.ru:
В этом месяце мы представляем Хану, которая работает в нашем отделе обслуживания клиентов.

Хане за тридцать. Она среднего роста, стройная, с короткими кудрявыми волосами. Говорят, внешне она похожа на маму, но по характеру она скорее в отца: тихая, терпеливая и очень надёжная. «С незнакомыми я довольно застенчива, — говорит она, — зато с друзьями разговорчива».

Хана родом из маленького городка на севере. Она живёт в квартире у реки вместе с сестрой. Они хорошо ладят, хотя общего у них мало: Хана аккуратная, а сестра — неряха!

Обычно Хана начинает работу в восемь. Она отвечает примерно на сорок писем в день и разговаривает с клиентами по телефону. Обедает за рабочим столом она редко: предпочитает прогуляться. Дважды в неделю она тренируется в беговом клубе и изредка участвует в забегах.

Сейчас Хана учит испанский. Она копит на долгий отпуск в Южной Америке, поэтому в последнее время редко ест вне дома. «Машины у меня нет, и одежду я почти не покупаю, — смеётся она. — Однако на книги трачу слишком много».

email.title: An e-mail to a host family
email.text:
Dear Mr and Mrs Reid,

My name is Pavel and I am going to stay with you in July. I would like to tell you something about myself.

I am twenty-four and I come from Brno. I work in a bank, but at the moment I am also doing an evening course in English, because I need it for my job. I am quite a quiet person, although I like meeting new people.

In my free time I play the piano and I go cycling every other day. I am keen on cooking too, so I am happy to help in the kitchen. I do not smoke and I am tidy.

I have two questions. How far is your house from the school? And what kind of food do you usually eat? I eat everything, but I do not like very spicy food.

I am looking forward to meeting you both.

Best wishes,
Pavel

tr.en: Summary: Pavel, 24, from Brno, works in a bank and is doing an evening English course for his job. He is quiet but likes meeting people. He plays the piano, cycles every other day and likes cooking; he doesn't smoke and is tidy. He asks how far the house is from the school and what kind of food the family eats; he doesn't like very spicy food. He will stay with the Reids in July.
tr.ru:
Уважаемые мистер и миссис Рид!

Меня зовут Павел, и в июле я буду жить у вас. Я хотел бы немного рассказать о себе.

Мне двадцать четыре года, я из Брно. Я работаю в банке, а сейчас ещё хожу на вечерние курсы английского, потому что он нужен мне для работы. Я довольно тихий человек, хотя люблю знакомиться с новыми людьми.

В свободное время я играю на пианино и через день катаюсь на велосипеде. Ещё я увлекаюсь готовкой, так что с удовольствием помогу на кухне. Я не курю и аккуратен.

У меня два вопроса. Как далеко ваш дом от школы? И какую еду вы обычно едите? Я ем всё, но не люблю очень острое.

С нетерпением жду встречи с вами обоими.

С наилучшими пожеланиями,
Павел

lessons.subtitle: Where do you come from? Whose guitar is that?

text.en: In most questions the order is **Q**uestion word – **A**uxiliary (do / does / is / are) – **S**ubject – **V**erb: *Where **do** you **live**?* · *What **does** she **do**?* · *Why **are** you **laughing**?*
text.ru: В большинстве вопросов порядок такой: **вопросительное слово – вспомогательный глагол (do / does / is / are) – подлежащее – смысловой глагол**: *Where **do** you **live**?* · *What **does** she **do**?* · *Why **are** you **laughing**?* Русское «Где ты живёшь?» без вспомогательного глагола по-английски не работает: ~~Where you live?~~

text.en: When the main verb is **be**, do not add *do*: *Where **is** the station?* · *How old **are** you?* · *Who **is** that man?*
text.ru: Если главный глагол — **be**, *do* не нужен: *Where **is** the station?* · *How old **are** you?* · *Who **is** that man?* Ошибка: ~~Where does the station is?~~

h.en: Who cooks? — questions about the subject

text.en: When **who** or **what** is the subject, there is no *do / does*, and the verb takes *-s*: ***Who cooks** in this flat?* · ***What happens** next?* Compare: *Who **do you live** with?* (who = object).
text.ru: Когда **who** или **what** — подлежащее, *do / does* не нужен, а глагол получает *-s*: ***Who cooks** in this flat?* · ***What happens** next?* Сравните: *Who **do you live** with?* (здесь who — дополнение). Русское «Кто готовит?» — *Who cooks?*, а не ~~Who does cook?~~

text.en: **Which** — a choice from a small number: *Which room is mine?* **Whose** — the owner: *Whose guitar is that?* **What kind of** — the type: *What kind of music do you like?*
text.ru: **Which** — выбор из небольшого числа: *Which room is mine?* **Whose** — чей: *Whose guitar is that?* **What kind of** — какого рода: *What kind of music do you like?* Не путайте *whose* (чей) и *who's* (= who is).

text.en: ***How long*** (time) · ***how far*** (distance) · ***how often*** (frequency) · ***how old*** (age) · ***how many*** + plural · ***how much*** + uncountable or price.
text.ru: ***How long*** (как долго) · ***how far*** (как далеко) · ***how often*** (как часто) · ***how old*** (сколько лет) · ***how many*** + множественное число · ***how much*** + неисчисляемое или цена.

lessons.subtitle: I work in a bank, but this week I'm studying.

text.en: **Present simple** — habits, facts, things that are always true: *I **work** in a bank.* **Present continuous** (*am / is / are + -ing*) — now, or around now, and temporary: *This week I**'m studying** for an exam.*
text.ru: **Present simple** — привычки, факты, то, что верно всегда: *I **work** in a bank.* **Present continuous** (*am / is / are + -ing*) — сейчас или в этот период, временно: *This week I**'m studying** for an exam.* В русском оба случая — просто «работаю», «учусь», поэтому время приходится выбирать по смыслу.

table: She's living with friends this month. (temporary)

text.en: Simple: *always, usually, often, every day, once a week, never.* Continuous: ***now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, these days***.
text.ru: Simple: *always, usually, often, every day, once a week, never.* Continuous: ***now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, these days***.

text.en: Some verbs describe a state, not an action, and are not normally used in the continuous: ***know, understand, believe, remember, like, love, hate, want, need, prefer, mean, belong, seem, own, agree***. *I **know** him.* (not ~~I'm knowing~~) · *This bag **belongs** to me.*
text.ru: Некоторые глаголы обозначают состояние, а не действие, и обычно не употребляются в continuous: ***know, understand, believe, remember, like, love, hate, want, need, prefer, mean, belong, seem, own, agree***. *I **know** him.* (не ~~I'm knowing~~) · *This bag **belongs** to me.* Даже если по-русски «я сейчас понимаю» — *I understand now*.

text.en: **have** = own → simple only: *I **have** a car.* **have** = eat, take, experience → both: *I**'m having** lunch.* · *We**'re having** a great time.*
text.ru: **have** = иметь → только simple: *I **have** a car.* **have** = есть, принимать, проводить → оба времени: *I**'m having** lunch.* · *We**'re having** a great time.*

text.en: *I **think** it's a good idea.* (= my opinion → simple) · *I**'m thinking** about the kitchen.* (= it's in my head now → continuous)
text.ru: *I **think** it's a good idea.* (= моё мнение → simple) · *I**'m thinking** about the kitchen.* (= размышляю сейчас → continuous)

text.en: *always, usually, often, sometimes, occasionally, rarely, hardly ever, never* go **before the main verb** but **after be**: *She **rarely eats** at her desk.* · *He **is never** late.* · *I **don't often** go out.*
text.ru: *always, usually, often, sometimes, occasionally, rarely, hardly ever, never* стоят **перед смысловым глаголом**, но **после be**: *She **rarely eats** at her desk.* · *He **is never** late.* · *I **don't often** go out.* В русском место свободное («я редко ем», «ем я редко»), в английском — нет.

text.en: Longer expressions go at the **end**: *I go to the gym **twice a week**.* · *We eat out **once a month**.* · *She calls her mother **every other day**.* · *He complains **all the time**.*
text.ru: Длинные выражения ставятся в **конец**: *I go to the gym **twice a week**.* · *We eat out **once a month**.* · *She calls her mother **every other day**.* · *He complains **all the time**.*

text.en: 1 × = **once**, 2 × = **twice**, then ***three times, four times*** … + **a** day / week / month / year: *three times **a** week* (not ~~in a week~~, not ~~per week~~ in everyday speech).
text.ru: 1 раз = **once**, 2 раза = **twice**, дальше ***three times, four times*** … + **a** day / week / month / year: *three times **a** week* (не ~~in a week~~). Слова «one time», «two times» возможны, но обычно говорят *once, twice*.

text.en: These words are already negative, so the verb stays positive: *I **never drink** coffee.* (not ~~I don't never~~) · *He **hardly ever calls**.*

text.en: **also** goes before the main verb (after *be*): *I **also** play the piano.* · *She **is also** a good cook.* **too** goes at the end: *I play the piano **too**.*
text.ru: **also** ставится перед смысловым глаголом (после *be*): *I **also** play the piano.* · *She **is also** a good cook.* **too** — в конце: *I play the piano **too**.* В отрицании вместо *too* — *either*: *I don't smoke **either**.*

text.en: **but** joins two parts in one sentence: *I'm quiet, **but** I like parties.* **However** starts a new sentence, with a comma: *I'm quiet. **However,** I like parties.* **although** goes before the less important fact: ***Although** I'm quiet, I like parties.* / *I like parties, **although** I'm quiet.*
text.ru: **but** соединяет две части одного предложения: *I'm quiet, **but** I like parties.* **However** начинает новое предложение, после него запятая: *I'm quiet. **However,** I like parties.* **although** («хотя») ставится перед менее важным фактом: ***Although** I'm quiet, I like parties.* / *I like parties, **although** I'm quiet.* Нельзя в одном предложении *although … but …*.

text.en: **because** + reason: *I'm learning English **because** I need it for my job.* **so** + result: *I need English for my job, **so** I'm doing a course.*
text.ru: **because** + причина: *I'm learning English **because** I need it for my job.* **so** + следствие: *I need English for my job, **so** I'm doing a course.*

text.en: *We **both** work in a bank.* (before the main verb) · *We **are both** tidy.* (after be) · ***Both** my parents are teachers.* · *I'm looking forward to meeting you **both**.*
text.ru: *We **both** work in a bank.* (перед смысловым глаголом) · *We **are both** tidy.* (после be) · ***Both** my parents are teachers.* · *I'm looking forward to meeting you **both**.*

text.en: Each adjective has its own preposition, and a verb after it takes **-ing**: *I'm **interested in** history.* · *She's **keen on** cook**ing**.* · *He's **good at** explain**ing** things.*
text.ru: У каждого прилагательного свой предлог, а глагол после него — с **-ing**: *I'm **interested in** history.* · *She's **keen on** cook**ing**.* · *He's **good at** explain**ing** things.* Русские «интересуюсь историей», «увлекаюсь готовкой» — творительный падеж, а в английском — разные предлоги, их нужно запоминать.

weekend.title: How was your weekend?
weekend.text:
Nina: Hi, Omar! How was your weekend?
Omar: It was great, thanks. I went to the coast with my cousins.
Nina: Lucky you! Did you drive there?
Omar: No, we didn't. We took the train. It was only an hour and a half.
Nina: What did you do there?
Omar: We walked along the beach, ate fish and chips and visited a small museum. What about you? Were you at home?
Nina: No, I wasn't. I was at my sister's. She moved to a new flat last week, so I helped her.
Omar: Did you carry all the boxes?
Nina: I carried about thirty! I didn't sleep well on Saturday because my back hurt.
Omar: Poor you. Did she say thank you?
Nina: She did. She cooked a lovely dinner and gave me a plant for my kitchen.
Omar: That was kind of her. When did you get back?
Nina: Late last night. I didn't hear my alarm this morning, and I missed my bus!

tr.en: Summary: Omar went to the coast with his cousins by train (an hour and a half). They walked along the beach, ate fish and chips and visited a small museum. Nina was at her sister's: her sister moved to a new flat last week and Nina helped — she carried about thirty boxes and didn't sleep well because her back hurt. Her sister cooked dinner and gave her a plant. Nina got back late last night, didn't hear her alarm and missed her bus.

holiday.title: The worst journey — and the best holiday
holiday.text:
Last summer my friend Rosa and I decided to go to a small village on the coast of Croatia. We booked the flights in March and planned everything very carefully. But the journey didn't go as we planned!

First, we arrived at the airport early, at six in the morning. Then we heard the bad news: there was a storm, and our flight had a delay of five hours. We sat in a café, drank too much coffee and read all our magazines.

After that, we finally got on the plane. The flight was fine, but when we landed, my suitcase wasn't there. I waited for an hour, but it didn't come. Unfortunately, all my summer clothes were in it.

Later, we took a bus to the village. It was dark when we arrived, and we couldn't find the house. Suddenly a dog began to bark, and an old woman came out of a door. Luckily, she knew the owner of our house, and she walked there with us.

In the end, everything was fine. My suitcase arrived two days later. We swam every morning, ate wonderful food and met some very friendly people. It was the worst journey of my life — and the best holiday.

tr.en: Summary: Last summer the writer and her friend Rosa went to a village on the coast of Croatia. They booked the flights in March. At the airport (they arrived at 6 a.m.) there was a storm and a five-hour delay. After the flight the writer's suitcase with all her summer clothes was missing. They took a bus and arrived in the dark; they couldn't find the house until an old woman, who knew the owner, walked there with them. The suitcase came two days later. They swam every morning, ate well and met friendly people: the worst journey, the best holiday.
tr.ru:
Прошлым летом мы с подругой Розой решили поехать в маленькую деревню на побережье Хорватии. Билеты на самолёт мы забронировали в марте и всё очень тщательно спланировали. Но дорога прошла совсем не по плану!

Сначала мы приехали в аэропорт рано, в шесть утра. Потом услышали плохую новость: была гроза, и наш рейс задержали на пять часов. Мы сидели в кафе, выпили слишком много кофе и прочитали все свои журналы.

После этого мы наконец сели в самолёт. Перелёт прошёл нормально, но, когда мы приземлились, моего чемодана не оказалось. Я ждала час, но он так и не появился. К сожалению, в нём была вся моя летняя одежда.

Позже мы поехали в деревню на автобусе. Когда мы приехали, было темно, и мы не могли найти дом. Вдруг залаяла собака, и из двери вышла пожилая женщина. К счастью, она знала хозяина нашего дома и проводила нас.

В конце концов всё закончилось хорошо. Чемодан привезли через два дня. Мы купались каждое утро, ели чудесную еду и познакомились с очень приветливыми людьми. Это была худшая дорога в моей жизни — и лучший отпуск.

life.title: My grandmother's story
life.text:
My grandmother, Elena, was born in 1941 in a small village in the mountains. She had four brothers and she was the only girl. Her childhood wasn't easy: the family didn't have much money, and the children walked five kilometres to school.

Elena loved books. At the age of seventeen she left the village and moved to the city. She worked in a shop during the day and studied in the evening. Four years later she graduated and became a teacher of mathematics.

In the 1960s she met my grandfather at a dance. He was a bus driver, and he couldn't dance at all! They got married a year later and had two children: my mother and my uncle.

My grandmother taught at the same school for thirty-five years. She knew every family in the town. She retired in 1999, but she didn't stop working: she began to teach children from poor families at home, and she never took any money for it.

She died three years ago, at the age of eighty. I still have her old maths books. When I open them, I remember her voice: “Don't be afraid of mistakes. Be afraid of doing nothing.”

tr.en: Summary: Elena, the writer's grandmother, was born in 1941 in a mountain village; she had four brothers. The family was poor, and the children walked five kilometres to school. At seventeen she moved to the city, worked in a shop, studied in the evening, graduated four years later and became a maths teacher. In the 1960s she met her husband, a bus driver, at a dance; they married a year later and had two children. She taught at the same school for thirty-five years, retired in 1999 and then taught poor children at home for free. She died three years ago, aged eighty.
tr.ru:
Моя бабушка Елена родилась в 1941 году в маленькой горной деревне. У неё было четыре брата, и она была единственной девочкой. Детство у неё было нелёгким: денег в семье было мало, а в школу дети ходили пешком за пять километров.

Елена любила книги. В семнадцать лет она уехала из деревни и перебралась в город. Днём она работала в магазине, а вечером училась. Через четыре года она окончила институт и стала учительницей математики.

В 1960-е годы она познакомилась на танцах с моим дедушкой. Он был водителем автобуса и совсем не умел танцевать! Через год они поженились, и у них родилось двое детей: моя мама и мой дядя.

Бабушка тридцать пять лет преподавала в одной и той же школе. Она знала каждую семью в городе. В 1999 году она вышла на пенсию, но работать не перестала: начала заниматься дома с детьми из бедных семей и никогда не брала за это денег.

Она умерла три года назад, в возрасте восьмидесяти лет. У меня до сих пор хранятся её старые учебники математики. Когда я их открываю, я вспоминаю её голос: «Не бойся ошибок. Бойся ничего не делать».

title.en: I was, we stayed: be and regular verbs
title.ru: I was, we stayed: be и правильные глаголы

lessons.subtitle: It was great. We walked along the beach.

text.en: **I / he / she / it was** · **you / we / they were**. Negative: **wasn't / weren't**. Question: *Were you at home?* — *Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.*
text.ru: **I / he / she / it was** · **you / we / they were**. Отрицание: **wasn't / weren't**. Вопрос: *Were you at home?* — *Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.* С *was / were* вспомогательный *did* не нужен: ~~Did you be at home?~~

text.en: Most verbs add **-ed**, and the form is the same for all persons: *I walk**ed**, she walk**ed**, they walk**ed**.*
text.ru: Большинство глаголов получают **-ed**, и форма одна для всех лиц: *I walk**ed**, she walk**ed**, they walk**ed**.* Никакого *-s* в третьем лице: ~~she walkeds~~.

text.en: Four small rules.
text.ru: Четыре небольших правила.

text.en: After **t** or **d** it is a new syllable /ɪd/: *visit-ed, decid-ed, want-ed.* After other sounds there is **no extra syllable**: *walked* /t/, *stayed* /d/, *stopped* /t/, *arrived* /d/.
text.ru: После **t** или **d** появляется лишний слог /ɪd/: *visit-ed, decid-ed, want-ed.* После остальных звуков **лишнего слога нет**: *walked* /t/, *stayed* /d/, *stopped* /t/, *arrived* /d/. Не произносите ~~«уок-ед»~~, ~~«стоп-ед»~~.

text.en: In British English verbs ending in **-l** double it: *travel → trave**ll**ed*, *cancel → cance**ll**ed*.
text.ru: В британском английском глаголы на **-l** удваивают её: *travel → trave**ll**ed*, *cancel → cance**ll**ed* (в американском — *traveled*).

title.ru: I went, I saw: неправильные глаголы

lessons.subtitle: We took the train and ate fish and chips.

text.en: About 150 common verbs do not take *-ed*. Each has its own past form, the same for all persons: *I **went**, she **went**, they **went**.* You have to learn them — but they are the verbs you use most.
text.ru: Около 150 употребительных глаголов не принимают *-ed*. У каждого своя форма прошедшего времени, одинаковая для всех лиц: *I **went**, she **went**, they **went**.* Их приходится учить, но это самые нужные глаголы.

text.en: Verbs with similar changes are easier to remember together.
text.ru: Глаголы с похожими изменениями легче запоминать вместе.

table: buy → bought · think → thought · teach → taught
drink → drank · begin → began · run → ran (u → a)
leave → left · sleep → slept · meet → met
write → wrote · speak → spoke · break → broke · wake → woke
know → knew · see → saw · fall → fell
read → read /red/ · put → put · cut → cut

text.en: *go → **went*** · *come → **came*** · *have → **had*** · *do → **did*** · *get → **got*** · *make → **made*** · *take → **took*** · *give → **gave*** · *say → **said*** /sed/ · *tell → **told***.
text.ru: *go → **went*** · *come → **came*** · *have → **had*** · *do → **did*** · *get → **got*** · *make → **made*** · *take → **took*** · *give → **gave*** · *say → **said*** (читается /sed/) · *tell → **told***.

text.en: **say** something (to somebody): *She **said** thank you.* **tell** somebody something: *She **told me** the news.* After *tell* you need a person.
text.ru: **say** что-то (кому-то): *She **said** thank you.* **tell** кому-то что-то: *She **told me** the news.* После *tell* обязательно нужен человек: ~~She told that…~~ → *She told **me** that…* или *She **said** that…*

text.en: **lose — lost**: not have any more: *I **lost** my wallet.* **miss — missed**: be too late for: *I **missed** the bus.*
text.ru: **lose — lost**: потерять: *I **lost** my wallet.* **miss — missed**: опоздать на что-то, пропустить: *I **missed** the bus.* По-русски «потерял автобус» не говорят, по-английски тоже: ~~I lost the bus~~.

text.en: In questions and negatives the past is shown by **did / didn't**, and the main verb goes back to the **base form**: *Did you **go**?* (not ~~Did you went?~~) · *I didn't **see** her.* (not ~~didn't saw~~)
text.ru: В вопросах и отрицаниях прошедшее время показывает **did / didn't**, а смысловой глагол возвращается в **начальную форму**: *Did you **go**?* (не ~~Did you went?~~) · *I didn't **see** her.* (не ~~didn't saw~~). Прошедшее время отмечается один раз.

table: Did she go to Paris? — Yes, she did. / No, she didn't.
Where did she go? · What did she see?

text.en: When **who** or **what** is the subject, there is no *did*: ***Who went** with you?* · ***What happened**?* Compare: *Who **did you meet**?*
text.ru: Когда **who** или **what** — подлежащее, *did* не нужен: ***Who went** with you?* · ***What happened**?* Сравните: *Who **did you meet**?* (кого вы встретили?)

text.en: **ago** goes **after** the period: *two days **ago*** · *a year **ago*** · *ten minutes **ago***. *How long ago did you arrive?*
text.ru: **ago** ставится **после** отрезка времени: *two days **ago*** · *a year **ago*** · *ten minutes **ago***. По-русски «два дня назад» — порядок тот же, но не говорите ~~ago two days~~ и ~~before two days~~.

text.en: ***last** night / week / month / year / Monday* — no preposition, no article (not ~~in the last week~~). ***yesterday** morning / afternoon / evening*, but ***last night***. ***in** 2019 · **in** March · **on** Monday · **on** 5 May · **at** six o'clock*.
text.ru: ***last** night / week / month / year / Monday* — без предлога и без артикля (не ~~in the last week~~). ***yesterday** morning / afternoon / evening*, но ***last night*** (не ~~yesterday night~~). ***in** 2019 · **in** March · **on** Monday · **on** 5 May · **at** six o'clock*.

text.en: ***When I was** a child, I lived in a village.* · ***When I was** twenty, I moved to the city.* A comma follows if the *when*-part comes first.
text.ru: ***When I was** a child, I lived in a village.* · ***When I was** twenty, I moved to the city.* Если часть с *when* стоит первой, после неё ставится запятая.

lessons.subtitle: First… Then… Suddenly… In the end…

text.en: ***First,** … **Then** … **After that,** … **Later,** … **Finally,** / **In the end,** …* They usually stand at the beginning of the sentence, often with a comma.
text.ru: ***First,** … **Then** … **After that,** … **Later,** … **Finally,** / **In the end,** …* Обычно они стоят в начале предложения, часто с запятой.

text.en: **then** needs no comma: *Then we got on the plane.* **after that** is a little stronger. Do not say ~~after, we went~~ — *after* needs a noun or *that*: ***After the film,** we went home.* · ***After that,** we went home.*
text.ru: **then** — без запятой: *Then we got on the plane.* **after that** звучит чуть сильнее. Нельзя сказать ~~after, we went~~ — после *after* нужно существительное или *that*: ***After the film,** we went home.* · ***After that,** we went home.* Русское «после мы пошли» — это *after that* или *then*.

h.en: finally, in the end, at the end
h.ru: finally, in the end, at the end

text.en: **Finally** — the last action in a list, or “at last”. **In the end** — the result after problems: *In the end, everything was fine.* **At the end of** + noun — the last part: *at the end of the film*.
text.ru: **Finally** — последнее действие в ряду или «наконец-то». **In the end** — итог после трудностей: *In the end, everything was fine.* **At the end of** + существительное — последняя часть: *at the end of the film*. Не путайте *in the end* (в итоге) и *at the end* (в конце чего-то).

text.en: They show your feeling about the fact: ***Luckily,** she knew the owner.* · ***Unfortunately,** all my clothes were in the suitcase.*
text.ru: Они показывают ваше отношение к факту: ***Luckily,** she knew the owner.* · ***Unfortunately,** all my clothes were in the suitcase.*

text.en: A **journey** is the travelling itself, from A to B: *The journey took five hours.* A **trip** is going somewhere and coming back: *a business trip, a day trip.* **travel** is usually a verb: *I travel a lot.* **luggage** is uncountable: *a lot of luggage*, *two pieces of luggage* (not ~~luggages~~).
text.ru: **journey** — сам путь из A в B: *The journey took five hours.* **trip** — поездка туда и обратно: *a business trip, a day trip.* **travel** обычно глагол: *I travel a lot.* **luggage** неисчисляемое: *a lot of luggage*, *two pieces of luggage* (не ~~luggages~~).

text.en: *I **was born** in 1998.* · *She **was born** in a small village.* It is always **was / were born** — never ~~I born~~ and never ~~I am born~~ for the past.
text.ru: *I **was born** in 1998.* · *She **was born** in a small village.* Всегда **was / were born** — не ~~I born~~ и не ~~I am born~~ о прошлом. Вопрос: *Where **were** you **born**?*

text.en: *be born → grow up → go to school → leave school → go to university → **graduate** → get a job → **get married** → have children → **retire** → **die***.
text.ru: *be born → grow up → go to school → leave school → go to university → **graduate** → get a job → **get married** → have children → **retire** → **die***. *get married **to** somebody* (не ~~with~~): *She got married to a bus driver.*

text.en: ***at the age of** seventeen* · ***when she was** seventeen* · ***in** 1999* · ***in the 1960s*** · ***four years later*** · ***for** thirty-five years* (how long) · ***three years ago***.
text.ru: ***at the age of** seventeen* · ***when she was** seventeen* · ***in** 1999* · ***in the 1960s*** (в шестидесятые) · ***four years later*** (через четыре года — в рассказе о прошлом) · ***for** thirty-five years* (как долго) · ***three years ago*** (три года назад — от сегодняшнего дня).

text.en: **ago** counts back from **now**: *She died three years ago.* **later** counts forward from a **point in the story**: *She moved in 1958. Four years later, she graduated.*
text.ru: **ago** отсчитывает назад от **настоящего момента**: *She died three years ago.* **later** отсчитывает вперёд от **момента в рассказе**: *She moved in 1958. Four years later, she graduated.* Русское «через четыре года» в прошлом — *four years later*, а не ~~after four years ago~~.

text.en: *She **became** a teacher.* (= she started to be one) — an article is needed with jobs: *a teacher, an engineer*.
text.ru: *She **became** a teacher.* (= стала учительницей) — с профессиями нужен артикль: *a teacher, an engineer*. Не ~~She became teacher~~.

tasks.sample:
My aunt Vera was born in 1962 in a small town near the sea. She grew up in a house with a big garden, and her childhood was very happy. At the age of eighteen she moved to the capital and studied medicine. Six years later she graduated and became a children's doctor.

She worked in the same hospital for thirty years. She got married in 1990 and had one son, my cousin. She retired four years ago, but she didn't stop helping people: every week she visited old neighbours and checked their health.

She always said, “A good doctor listens first.” I think that is true for everybody.

powercut.title: The night the lights went out
powercut.text:
One evening last winter I was at home alone. It was snowing outside and the wind was blowing hard. I was sitting on the sofa and reading a detective story, and my cat was sleeping next to me.

Suddenly, while I was reading the most frightening page, all the lights went out. At first I thought it was just my flat, but when I looked out of the window, the whole street was dark. It was a power cut.

I couldn't find my torch, so I lit a candle. As I was walking to the kitchen, I heard a noise upstairs. Somebody was moving a chair! But I live on the top floor, and there is nothing above my flat — only the roof.

I was really frightened. I stood still and listened. The noise stopped. Then, a few minutes later, somebody knocked at my door. I didn't open it. “Who is it?” I whispered.

“It's Mr Novak from next door,” a voice said. “I was fixing my aerial on the roof when the lights went out. I couldn't see anything, and I dropped my keys. Have you got a torch?”

I was so relieved that I began to laugh. We found the torch together — it was in the fridge. Don't ask me why.

tr.en: Summary: One winter evening the writer was at home alone; it was snowing, she was reading a detective story and her cat was sleeping. While she was reading, the lights went out — a power cut in the whole street. She couldn't find her torch and lit a candle. As she was walking to the kitchen she heard somebody moving a chair above her, though she lives on the top floor. She was frightened. A few minutes later somebody knocked: it was her neighbour Mr Novak, who was fixing his aerial on the roof when the lights went out and dropped his keys. She was relieved and laughed. The torch was in the fridge.
tr.ru:
Однажды вечером прошлой зимой я была дома одна. На улице шёл снег и дул сильный ветер. Я сидела на диване и читала детектив, а рядом спала кошка.

Вдруг, когда я читала самую страшную страницу, погас весь свет. Сначала я подумала, что это только у меня в квартире, но, выглянув в окно, увидела, что вся улица тёмная. Отключили электричество.

Я не могла найти фонарик и зажгла свечу. Когда я шла на кухню, наверху послышался шум. Кто-то двигал стул! Но я живу на последнем этаже, и над моей квартирой ничего нет — только крыша.

Мне стало по-настоящему страшно. Я замерла и прислушалась. Шум прекратился. Потом, через несколько минут, в дверь постучали. Я не открыла. «Кто там?» — прошептала я.

«Это господин Новак, ваш сосед, — сказал голос. — Я чинил на крыше антенну, когда погас свет. Ничего не было видно, и я уронил ключи. У вас есть фонарик?»

Мне стало так легко, что я рассмеялась. Фонарик мы нашли вместе — он лежал в холодильнике. Не спрашивайте почему.

accident.title: What did you see?
accident.text:
Police officer: Good morning. You saw the accident, didn't you? Can you tell me what happened?
Witness: Yes, of course. I was waiting at the bus stop on the corner.
Police officer: What time was that?
Witness: About ten past eight. It was raining, so I was standing under the roof of the shop.
Police officer: What was the cyclist doing?
Witness: He was riding along the road, quite fast. He was wearing a dark jacket, and he wasn't using any lights.
Police officer: And the car?
Witness: The car was coming out of the car park. The driver was looking to the right, I think. She didn't see the cyclist.
Police officer: What happened next?
Witness: The cyclist tried to stop, but the road was wet, and he slipped. He hit the side of the car and fell on the pavement.
Police officer: Was he badly hurt?
Witness: He cut his hand and hurt his knee, but he could stand up. The driver got out at once and called an ambulance.
Police officer: Were the traffic lights working?
Witness: Yes, they were. They were green for the cyclist.
Police officer: Thank you. That's very helpful.

tr.en: Summary: A witness tells the police what she saw at about ten past eight. She was waiting at the bus stop on the corner, standing under the roof of a shop because it was raining. The cyclist was riding fast, wearing a dark jacket, without lights. A car was coming out of the car park; the driver was looking to the right and didn't see him. He tried to stop, slipped on the wet road, hit the side of the car and fell on the pavement. He cut his hand and hurt his knee but could stand up. The driver called an ambulance. The traffic lights were green for the cyclist.
tr.ru:
Полицейский: Доброе утро. Вы ведь видели аварию? Расскажите, что произошло.
Свидетельница: Да, конечно. Я ждала на автобусной остановке на углу.
Полицейский: Во сколько это было?
Свидетельница: Примерно в десять минут девятого. Шёл дождь, и я стояла под козырьком магазина.
Полицейский: Что делал велосипедист?
Свидетельница: Он ехал по дороге, довольно быстро. На нём была тёмная куртка, и ехал он без фонарей.
Полицейский: А машина?
Свидетельница: Машина выезжала с парковки. По-моему, женщина за рулём смотрела направо. Велосипедиста она не увидела.
Полицейский: Что было дальше?

wedding.title: The speech
wedding.text:
My brother got married last June, and he asked me to give a speech at the wedding. I was excited, but also very worried, because I am not a confident speaker.

On the day, everything was going well. The sun was shining, the guests were chatting and laughing, and a small band was playing in the garden. I was sitting next to my aunt, and I was reading my speech again and again.

Then my moment came. As I was walking to the front, I realised that the paper in my hand was not my speech. It was my shopping list! By the time I noticed, everybody was looking at me. I couldn't go back.

At first I was so embarrassed that I couldn't say a word. Then I decided to tell the truth. “I wrote a beautiful speech,” I said, “but it is at home, on my fridge. Here I have only this: milk, eggs, washing powder.”

To my surprise, everybody began to laugh, and my brother laughed more than anybody. So I spoke without notes — about our childhood, about the day he met his wife, about how happy he looked. It turned out to be the best speech of my life.

tr.en: Summary: The writer's brother got married last June and asked for a speech. The writer was excited but worried. On the day the sun was shining, the guests were chatting, a band was playing, and the writer was reading the speech again and again. Walking to the front, the writer realised the paper was a shopping list; everybody was looking. At first too embarrassed to speak, the writer told the truth — and everybody laughed. The writer then spoke without notes about their childhood and the couple, and it turned out to be the best speech ever.
tr.ru:
В июне прошлого года мой брат женился и попросил меня произнести речь на свадьбе. Я была в предвкушении, но и очень волновалась, потому что выступаю неуверенно.

В тот день всё шло хорошо. Светило солнце, гости болтали и смеялись, а в саду играл небольшой оркестр. Я сидела рядом с тётей и снова и снова перечитывала свою речь.

Потом настал мой черёд. Когда я шла вперёд, я поняла, что листок у меня в руке — не речь. Это был список покупок! К тому времени, как я это заметила, все уже смотрели на меня. Вернуться было нельзя.

Сначала мне было так неловко, что я не могла вымолвить ни слова. Потом решила сказать правду. «Я написала прекрасную речь, — сказала я, — но она осталась дома, на холодильнике. А здесь у меня только это: молоко, яйца, стиральный порошок».

К моему удивлению, все рассмеялись, а брат — громче всех. И я заговорила без бумажки: о нашем детстве, о дне, когда он познакомился с женой, о том, каким счастливым он выглядит. Оказалось, что это лучшая речь в моей жизни.

title.en: I was reading: the past continuous

lessons.subtitle: At nine o'clock I was sitting on the sofa.

text.en: **I / he / she / it was** read**ing** · **you / we / they were** read**ing**. Negative: *wasn't / weren't …ing*. Question: ***Were** you sleep**ing**?* — *Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.*
text.ru: **I / he / she / it was** read**ing** · **you / we / they were** read**ing**. Отрицание: *wasn't / weren't …ing*. Вопрос: ***Were** you sleep**ing**?* — *Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.* Это то же, что present continuous, только *am / is / are* заменены на *was / were*.

table: I was reading. · They were chatting.
I wasn't reading. · They weren't chatting.

h.en: Use: in the middle of an action

text.en: The action was **in progress at a moment in the past** — it started before and was not finished: *At nine o'clock I **was sitting** on the sofa.* · *This time yesterday we **were flying** to Rome.*
text.ru: Действие **было в процессе в определённый момент прошлого** — началось раньше и ещё не закончилось: *At nine o'clock I **was sitting** on the sofa.* · *This time yesterday we **were flying** to Rome.* По-русски это несовершенный вид: «сидел», «летели». Но не всякий несовершенный вид — past continuous: привычка в прошлом — past simple (*I walked to school every day*).

text.en: Stories often begin with it: *It **was snowing** and the wind **was blowing**. The guests **were chatting** and a band **was playing**.*
text.ru: С него часто начинаются рассказы: *It **was snowing** and the wind **was blowing**. The guests **were chatting** and a band **was playing**.* Это фон, на котором потом что-то произойдёт.

text.ru: Три правила.

lessons.subtitle: I was reading when the lights went out.

title.en: A long action and a short one

text.en: A long action was in progress (**past continuous**); a short action happened in the middle of it (**past simple**): *I **was reading when** the lights **went out**.* The long action may stop or continue.
text.ru: Долгое действие было в процессе (**past continuous**); короткое произошло посреди него (**past simple**): *I **was reading when** the lights **went out**.* Долгое действие при этом может прерваться или продолжиться. По-русски: «Я читал, когда погас свет» — несовершенный вид + совершенный.

text.en: You can turn the sentence round with **while** (or **as**) before the long action: ***While** I **was reading**, the lights **went out**.* Comma after the first part.
text.ru: Предложение можно перевернуть, поставив **while** (или **as**) перед долгим действием: ***While** I **was reading**, the lights **went out**.* После первой части — запятая. Запомните: **when** + короткое действие (simple), **while** + долгое (continuous).

text.en: Two actions in progress at the same time: ***While** I **was cooking**, my brother **was laying** the table.*
text.ru: Два действия шли одновременно: ***While** I **was cooking**, my brother **was laying** the table.*

text.en: If one thing happened **after** the other, both are simple: ***When** the lights **went out**, I **lit** a candle.* (first the lights, then the candle). Compare: *When the lights went out, I **was lighting** a candle.* (I was already doing it.)
text.ru: Если одно случилось **после** другого, оба глагола в simple: ***When** the lights **went out**, I **lit** a candle.* (сначала свет, потом свеча). Сравните: *When the lights went out, I **was lighting** a candle.* (я уже зажигал её в тот момент).

text.en: *I **cut** my finger.* · *She **burnt** her hand.* · *He **hurt** his knee.* · *I **dropped** my phone.* · *She **slipped** on the ice.* English uses **my / her / his** with parts of the body.
text.ru: *I **cut** my finger.* · *She **burnt** her hand.* · *He **hurt** his knee.* · *I **dropped** my phone.* · *She **slipped** on the ice.* С частями тела в английском нужны **my / her / his**: «порезал палец» — *cut **my** finger*, а не ~~cut the finger~~. *cut, hurt, hit* в прошедшем не меняются.

lessons.subtitle: He was riding fast. He slipped and fell.

text.en: **Past continuous** = the background, what was going on. **Past simple** = the events, what happened next, one after another: *He **was riding** fast. The road **was** wet. He **tried** to stop, **slipped** and **fell**.*
text.ru: **Past continuous** — фон, то, что происходило. **Past simple** — события, то, что случилось дальше, одно за другим: *He **was riding** fast. The road **was** wet. He **tried** to stop, **slipped** and **fell**.* По-русски цепочка событий — совершенный вид: «попытался, поскользнулся и упал».

text.en: With **for** + a period, or a number of times, use the simple: *I **waited for** an hour.* · *She **phoned** three times.* (not ~~was waiting for an hour~~ as a simple fact)
text.ru: С **for** + отрезок времени или с числом раз — simple: *I **waited for** an hour.* · *She **phoned** three times.* Русское «я ждал час» — несовершенный вид, но в английском это законченный факт: *I waited*.

text.en: *When I was a child, I **walked** to school every day.* (not ~~was walking~~)
text.ru: *When I was a child, I **walked** to school every day.* (не ~~was walking~~). Повторяющееся действие в прошлом — past simple, хотя по-русски «ходил».

text.en: As in the present: *know, want, like, believe, understand, have (= own), be*. *I **knew** the answer.* · *The road **was** wet.* · *She **had** a red bike.* (not ~~was knowing, was having a bike~~)
text.ru: Как и в настоящем: *know, want, like, believe, understand, have (= иметь), be*. *I **knew** the answer.* · *The road **was** wet.* · *She **had** a red bike.* (не ~~was knowing, was having a bike~~).

text.ru: Where were you? — *I **was waiting** at the bus stop.* What was he doing? — *He **was riding** along the road.* What happened? — *He **hit** the car and **fell** on the pavement.* Вопрос *What happened?* — всегда simple.

h.en: -ed for the person, -ing for the thing

text.en: **-ed** = how somebody feels: *I was **bored**.* **-ing** = what causes the feeling: *The film was **boring**.*
text.ru: **-ed** — что чувствует человек: *I was **bored**.* **-ing** — то, что вызывает чувство: *The film was **boring**.* Ошибка, меняющая смысл: *I'm boring* = «я скучный человек», а не «мне скучно».

text.en: **worried** (something bad may happen) → **relieved** (the worry has gone). **confused** (I don't understand). **annoyed** (a little angry). *I was **so** relieved **that** I began to laugh.*
text.ru: **worried** (может случиться плохое) → **relieved** (тревога ушла). **confused** (не понимаю). **annoyed** (слегка сердит). *I was **so** relieved **that** I began to laugh.* — «так …, что …».

text.en: **could** is the past of *can*: *I **couldn't** find my torch.* · *He **could** stand up.* · ***Could** you see anything?* After it — the base form, no *to*.
text.ru: **could** — прошедшее от *can*: *I **couldn't** find my torch.* · *He **could** stand up.* · ***Could** you see anything?* После него — начальная форма без *to*. С глаголами чувств (*see, hear, smell*) *could* особенно часто: *I could hear a noise.*

text.en: *“Who is it?” I **whispered**.* (very quietly) · *“Stop!” he **shouted**.* (very loudly) · *“It's me,” she **said**, and **smiled**.*
text.ru: *“Who is it?” I **whispered**.* (очень тихо) · *“Stop!” he **shouted**.* (очень громко) · *“It's me,” she **said**, and **smiled**.* В английском прямая речь — в кавычках “ ”, запятая стоит внутри кавычек.

lessons.subtitle: One evening last winter I was at home alone.

text.en: **1. The setting** — when, where, who, the weather, what was going on (past continuous): *One evening last winter I **was sitting** at home. It **was snowing**.* **2. The events** — what happened (past simple), with *suddenly, then, a few minutes later*. **3. The ending** — the result and your feeling: *It turned out that … I was so relieved.*
text.ru: **1. Обстановка** — когда, где, кто, погода, что происходило (past continuous): *One evening last winter I **was sitting** at home. It **was snowing**.* **2. События** — что случилось (past simple), со словами *suddenly, then, a few minutes later*. **3. Развязка** — итог и ваше чувство: *It turned out that … I was so relieved.*

text.en: ***One evening** last winter …* · ***One day** in June …* · ***A few years ago** …* · ***Last summer** something strange happened to me.*
text.ru: ***One evening** last winter …* · ***One day** in June …* · ***A few years ago** …* · ***Last summer** something strange happened to me.* «Однажды» — *one day / one evening*, а не ~~once day~~.

text.en: ***At first** I thought it was my flat. **Then** I looked out of the window.* · ***As soon as** I opened the door, the cat ran out.* · ***By the time** I noticed, everybody was looking at me.* · ***A few minutes later**, somebody knocked.*
text.ru: ***At first** I thought it was my flat. **Then** I looked out of the window.* · ***As soon as** I opened the door, the cat ran out.* (как только) · ***By the time** I noticed, everybody was looking at me.* (к тому времени как) · ***A few minutes later**, somebody knocked.* Не путайте *at first* (поначалу — потом всё изменилось) и *first* (сначала — первое в ряду действий).

text.en: ***To my surprise**, everybody began to laugh.* · ***It turned out** (that) it was my neighbour.* · ***It turned out to be** the best speech of my life.*
text.ru: ***To my surprise**, everybody began to laugh.* · ***It turned out** (that) it was my neighbour.* (оказалось, что) · ***It turned out to be** the best speech of my life.*

text.en: **still** = the action continued: *When I got home, it was **still** snowing.* It goes before the main verb, after *be*.
text.ru: **still** — действие продолжалось: *When I got home, it was **still** snowing.* Ставится перед смысловым глаголом, после *be*.

tasks.sample:
One evening last autumn I was coming home from work. It was getting dark, and a cold wind was blowing. I was walking through the park and listening to music when I noticed a small dog. It was following me.

At first I thought its owner was near, but nobody was there. The dog was wet and it was shaking. I was worried, so I took it home, gave it some food and put a photo on the internet.

The next morning somebody knocked at my door. To my surprise, it was my new neighbour from the third floor. “Is that my Bruno?” she asked. She was so relieved that she began to cry.

It turned out that Bruno often runs away. Now he visits me twice a week, and his owner and I are good friends.

travel.title: Have you ever…?
travel.text:
Nadia: Tom, have you ever been to Morocco?
Tom: No, I haven't. I've never been to Africa. Why?
Nadia: I'm planning a holiday. I've been to Spain and Portugal, but I want to see something different.
Tom: My sister has been to Morocco twice. She loved it.
Nadia: Really? What did she do there?
Tom: The first time she stayed in Marrakesh. The second time, two years ago, she went to the desert and rode a camel.
Nadia: I've never ridden a camel. Have you?
Tom: No, but I've ridden a horse. Once. I fell off after five minutes.
Nadia: Poor you! Have you ever tried Moroccan food?
Tom: Yes, I have. There's a good Moroccan restaurant near the station. I ate there last month.
Nadia: Was it good?
Tom: It was fantastic. I had lamb with apricots. I've never eaten anything like it.
Nadia: Then let's go there on Friday. You can tell me more about your sister's trips.
Tom: Good idea. I'll ask her for some photos.

tr.en: Summary: Nadia is planning a holiday and asks Tom about Morocco. Tom has never been to Africa; Nadia has been to Spain and Portugal. Tom's sister has been to Morocco twice: the first time she stayed in Marrakesh; the second time, two years ago, she went to the desert and rode a camel. Neither Nadia nor Tom has ridden a camel; Tom has ridden a horse once and fell off. Tom has tried Moroccan food: he ate at a restaurant near the station last month and had lamb with apricots. They decide to go there on Friday.

party.title: Are we ready?
party.text:
Mira: It's half past five. The guests are coming at seven. Are we ready?
Oskar: Nearly. I've already tidied the living room, and I've just put the drinks in the fridge.
Mira: Great. Have you bought the bread yet?
Oskar: Yes, I have. I bought it this morning. But I haven't made the salad yet.
Mira: Don't worry, I'll do it. Has Lena replied to the invitation?
Oskar: Yes, she's just sent a message. She's coming, and she's bringing a cake.
Mira: Lovely. What about your cousin?
Oskar: He hasn't replied yet. I've already written to him twice.
Mira: Oh no — the candles! I've forgotten the candles for the cake.
Oskar: No, you haven't. They're in the kitchen drawer. I found them yesterday.
Mira: Thank goodness. Have you chosen the music?
Oskar: Not yet. Can you do that while I make the salad?
Mira: You said I was making the salad!
Oskar: Did I? Then I've just changed my mind.

tr.en: Summary: At half past five Mira and Oskar check that they are ready for guests at seven. Oskar has already tidied the living room and has just put the drinks in the fridge. He bought the bread this morning but hasn't made the salad yet. Lena has just sent a message: she is coming with a cake. Oskar's cousin hasn't replied yet, though Oskar has written twice. Mira thinks she has forgotten the candles, but Oskar found them yesterday in the kitchen drawer. They haven't chosen the music yet.

news.title: An e-mail with news
news.text:
Hi Sofia,

How are things? I'm sorry I haven't written lately — a lot has happened!

Guess what: I've moved house. Three weeks ago I left my little room in the centre, and now I live in a flat near the river. It's bigger and quieter, and I've already met two of my neighbours. I haven't bought a sofa yet, so my guests sit on the floor.

I've got more news. I've passed my driving test! I failed it in March, but I took it again last Friday and passed. I haven't driven alone yet — I'm still a bit frightened.

Unfortunately, I've lost my phone, so I've got a new number. I left the old one on a train last week. Luckily, all my photos were on my laptop.

By the way, have you heard from Daniel? He has gone to Canada for six months. He sent me a postcard from Toronto.

Anyway, what about you? Have you finished your course yet? Write soon and tell me everything.

I'm looking forward to hearing from you.

Best wishes,
Alma

tr.en: Summary: Alma writes to Sofia with news. She has moved house: three weeks ago she left her room in the centre and now lives in a bigger, quieter flat near the river; she has already met two neighbours but hasn't bought a sofa yet. She has passed her driving test (she failed in March and passed last Friday) but hasn't driven alone yet. She has lost her phone — she left it on a train last week — and has a new number. Daniel has gone to Canada for six months. She asks whether Sofia has finished her course yet.
tr.ru:
Привет, София!

Как дела? Прости, что в последнее время не писала — столько всего произошло!

Представляешь, я переехала. Три недели назад я съехала из своей комнатки в центре и теперь живу в квартире у реки. Она больше и тише, и я уже познакомилась с двумя соседями. Диван я ещё не купила, так что гости сидят на полу.

Есть и другие новости. Я сдала экзамен по вождению! В марте я его провалила, но в прошлую пятницу пересдала — и сдала. Одна я ещё не ездила — пока страшновато.

К сожалению, я потеряла телефон, так что у меня новый номер. Старый я оставила в поезде на прошлой неделе. К счастью, все фотографии были на ноутбуке.

Кстати, тебе Даниэль не писал? Он уехал в Канаду на полгода. Прислал мне открытку из Торонто.

В общем, а как ты? Ты уже закончила свои курсы? Напиши скорее и расскажи всё.

Очень жду твоего письма.

Всего наилучшего,
Альма

h.en: Experience: at some time in your life

text.en: We say **that** it happened, not **when**: *I**'ve ridden** a horse.* · *She**'s won** a prize.* The time is “in my life until now”.
text.ru: Мы сообщаем, **что** это было, но не **когда**: *I**'ve ridden** a horse.* · *She**'s won** a prize.* Время — «за мою жизнь до этого момента».

text.en: ***Have** you **ever** flown in a helicopter?* (at any time) — *No, I**'ve never** flown in one.* Both go **before the participle**. *never* already makes the sentence negative: not ~~I haven't never~~.
text.ru: ***Have** you **ever** flown in a helicopter?* (когда-нибудь) — *No, I**'ve never** flown in one.* Оба слова стоят **перед причастием**. *never* уже делает предложение отрицательным: не ~~I haven't never~~ — в английском одно отрицание.

text.en: *I've been there **once / twice / three times / many times**.* · *It's the best film I**'ve ever seen**.*
text.ru: *I've been there **once / twice / three times / many times**.* · *It's the best film I**'ve ever seen**.* — «лучший фильм, который я когда-либо видел».

text.en: The present perfect also shows a **past action with a result now**: *I**'ve lost** my keys.* (= I can't find them now) · *She**'s tidied** the room.* (= it is tidy now)
text.ru: Present perfect также показывает **прошлое действие с результатом в настоящем**: *I**'ve lost** my keys.* (= сейчас не могу их найти) · *She**'s tidied** the room.* (= сейчас в комнате чисто). Спросите себя: важно «когда» или важно «что теперь»? Если «что теперь» — present perfect.

text.en: *She**'s just sent** a message.* · *I**'ve just had** lunch.* **just** goes between *have* and the participle.
text.ru: *She**'s just sent** a message.* · *I**'ve just had** lunch.* **just** стоит между *have* и причастием.

text.en: *I**'ve already tidied** the living room.* (you don't need to do it) — also between *have* and the participle, in **positive** sentences.
text.ru: *I**'ve already tidied** the living room.* (тебе не нужно этого делать) — тоже между *have* и причастием, в **утвердительных** предложениях.

text.en: In **questions** and **negatives**, at the **end**: ***Have** you **bought** the bread **yet**?* · *I **haven't made** the salad **yet**.* Short answer: *Not yet.*
text.ru: В **вопросах** и **отрицаниях**, в **конце** предложения: ***Have** you **bought** the bread **yet**?* · *I **haven't made** the salad **yet**.* Краткий ответ: *Not yet.* По-русски и *already*, и *yet* в вопросе — «уже»; и *yet* в отрицании, и *still* — «ещё». Смотрите на тип предложения.

h.en: been to = went and came back

text.en: *I**'ve been to** Canada.* — I visited it at some time; I am **not there now**.
text.ru: *I**'ve been to** Canada.* — я когда-то там побывал; сейчас я **не там**.

h.en: gone to = went and is still there
h.ru: gone to = уехал и ещё там

text.en: *Daniel **has gone to** Canada.* — he is **there now** (or on the way). So you can't say ~~I've gone to Canada~~ about your experience when you are here.
text.ru: *Daniel **has gone to** Canada.* — он **сейчас там** (или в пути). Поэтому о своём опыте, находясь здесь, нельзя сказать ~~I've gone to Canada~~. По-русски разница — «был / побывал» и «уехал».

text.en: With *been* in the meaning “visited”, use **to**: *Have you ever **been to** Paris?* (not ~~been in Paris~~ for a visit). *I've been **there** twice.* (no *to* before *there* / *here* / *abroad*)
text.ru: С *been* в значении «побывал» — предлог **to**: *Have you ever **been to** Paris?* (не ~~been in Paris~~, хотя по-русски «в Париже»). *I've been **there** twice.* — перед *there / here / abroad* предлога нет.

text.en: *come — came — **come***: *Has the taxi **come** yet?* · *leave — left — **left***: *She**'s** already **left**.* (= she isn't here now) · *He**'s back**.* / *He**'s away** this week.*
text.ru: *come — came — **come***: *Has the taxi **come** yet?* · *leave — left — **left***: *She**'s** already **left**.* (= её сейчас здесь нет) · *He**'s back**.* (вернулся) / *He**'s away** this week.* (в отъезде).

text.en: A **trip** = going and coming back, usually short (*a business trip*). A **journey** = the time on the road (*a three-hour journey*). **travel** is usually a verb: *I love travelling.*
text.ru: **trip** — поездка туда и обратно, обычно короткая (*a business trip*). **journey** — сама дорога (*a three-hour journey*). **travel** — обычно глагол: *I love travelling.* Русское «путешествие» может быть и *trip*, и *journey*.

lessons.subtitle: I've passed my test! I took it last Friday.

text.en: If you say or ask **when** — *yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago, when I was a child, What time…? When…?* — use the **past simple**: *I **took** the test **last Friday**.* (not ~~I've taken it last Friday~~)
text.ru: Если вы называете или спрашиваете, **когда** — *yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago, when I was a child, What time…? When…?* — нужен **past simple**: *I **took** the test **last Friday**.* (не ~~I've taken it last Friday~~). Это главное правило: present perfect не сочетается с указанием законченного времени.

table.en: no time, or time not finished
table.ru: времени нет или оно не закончилось

table: ever, never, just, already, yet, so far, recently, this week, today
I lost it on a train last week.
Have you ever been to Rome?

text.en: Give the news in the **present perfect**, then the details (when, where, how) in the **past simple**: *I**'ve passed** my driving test! I **failed** it in March, but I **took** it again last Friday.*
text.ru: Новость сообщают в **present perfect**, а подробности (когда, где, как) — в **past simple**: *I**'ve passed** my driving test! I **failed** it in March, but I **took** it again last Friday.* Так же в разговоре: *Have you ever been to Rome? — Yes, I have. — When **did** you **go**?*

text.en: *I**'ve had** three coffees **today**.* (today is not over) · *We**'ve had** two tests **this week**.* · *I**'ve read** four books **so far** this year.* But: *I **had** three coffees **yesterday**.*
text.ru: *I**'ve had** three coffees **today**.* (день ещё не кончился) · *We**'ve had** two tests **this week**.* · *I**'ve read** four books **so far** this year.* Но: *I **had** three coffees **yesterday**.*

text.en: A life that is finished → past simple: *My grandfather **visited** forty countries.* A life that goes on → present perfect: *My aunt **has visited** forty countries.*
text.ru: Жизнь закончилась → past simple: *My grandfather **visited** forty countries.* Жизнь продолжается → present perfect: *My aunt **has visited** forty countries.*

text.en: ***Guess what!** I've got a new job.* — ***Congratulations!** / Really? / That's great news!* · *I've failed my exam.* — *Oh no, **I'm sorry to hear that**.* **news** is singular: *The news **is** good.*
text.ru: ***Guess what!** I've got a new job.* — ***Congratulations!** / Really? / That's great news!* · *I've failed my exam.* — *Oh no, **I'm sorry to hear that**.* Слово **news** — в единственном числе: *The news **is** good.* Одна новость — *a piece of news*, не ~~a news~~.

Hi Pavel,

How are things? I'm sorry I haven't written lately. So much has happened!

Guess what: I've changed my job. I left the bank two months ago, and now I work for a small travel company. I've already been to Prague and Vienna on business trips.

I've also started Spanish lessons. I had my first class last Tuesday. I haven't learnt much yet, but I can order a coffee.

Unfortunately, I've broken my arm. I slipped on the ice last week, so I'm typing this with one hand. Luckily, it's the left one.

By the way, have you heard from Irina? She has gone to Lisbon for a year.

Anyway, what about you? Have you bought a flat yet? Write soon.

I'm looking forward to hearing from you.

Best wishes,
Misha

plans.title: Next year
plans.text:
Ines: So, Raj, it's the last day of December. Have you made any resolutions?
Raj: Yes, three. First, I'm going to get fit. I've already joined a gym.
Ines: Good for you! And the second?
Raj: I'm going to save up for a car. And I'm going to learn to drive, of course.
Ines: That's a lot of money.
Raj: I know. So I'm going to give up taxis and takeaway coffee.
Ines: I don't think you'll give up coffee.
Raj: You'll see. What about you? What are you going to do next year?
Ines: I'm going to apply for a job in Lisbon. My company is opening an office there in the spring.
Raj: Really? Do you think you'll get it?
Ines: I hope so. I've started Portuguese lessons. I'm sure the language will help.
Raj: Lisbon! I'll visit you. I promise.
Ines: You won't have any money — you're saving up for a car!
Raj: Then I'll drive there.
Ines: Raj, you haven't had a single lesson yet.
Raj: That's true. Wait — I'll book the first one right now.

tr.en: Summary: On the last day of December Raj tells Ines his three resolutions: he is going to get fit (he has already joined a gym), save up for a car and learn to drive, and give up taxis and takeaway coffee. Ines doesn't think he will give up coffee. Ines is going to apply for a job in Lisbon, where her company is opening an office in the spring; she has started Portuguese lessons and is sure the language will help. Raj promises to visit her — he'll drive there, although he hasn't had a lesson yet, so he decides to book the first one right now.

forecast.title: The weekend weather
forecast.text:
Good evening. Here is the weather forecast for the weekend.

Tomorrow, Saturday, will start cold and clear, with temperatures of about two degrees in the morning. It will be sunny until lunchtime, but clouds will arrive from the west in the afternoon, and there might be a few showers in the evening.

Sunday will be very different. It will be wet and windy all day, with heavy rain in the north. In the mountains the rain may turn to snow. There might be a storm on the coast on Sunday night, so please be careful if you are driving.

The good news is that it will be mild: the temperature won't fall below eight degrees.

Next week will probably be dry, but it is too early to be sure.

So — if you are planning a walk, go tomorrow morning. And on Sunday, don't forget your umbrella. You'll definitely need it.

tr.en: Summary: The forecast for the weekend. Saturday will start cold and clear, about two degrees in the morning; sunny until lunchtime, then clouds from the west, and there might be a few showers in the evening. Sunday will be wet and windy all day, with heavy rain in the north; in the mountains the rain may turn to snow, and there might be a storm on the coast on Sunday night. It will be mild — not below eight degrees. Next week will probably be dry. Advice: walk on Saturday morning; take an umbrella on Sunday.
tr.ru:
Добрый вечер. Прогноз погоды на выходные.

Завтра, в субботу, день начнётся с холодной и ясной погоды, утром около двух градусов. До обеда будет солнечно, но после полудня с запада придут облака, а вечером возможны кратковременные дожди.

Воскресенье будет совсем другим. Весь день дождливо и ветрено, на севере сильный дождь. В горах дождь может перейти в снег. В ночь на понедельник на побережье возможна буря, поэтому будьте осторожны за рулём.

Хорошая новость: будет тепло — температура не опустится ниже восьми градусов.

Следующая неделя, вероятно, будет сухой, но говорить наверняка пока рано.

Итак, если вы планируете прогулку, идите завтра утром. А в воскресенье не забудьте зонт. Он вам точно понадобится.

invite.title: Barbecue on Saturday?
invite.text:
Greta: Hi everyone! I'm having a barbecue on Saturday to celebrate my new job. It starts at five, in my garden. Would you like to come?

Luis: I'd love to! Congratulations again. Shall I bring anything?

Greta: Thanks, Luis. Just bring something to drink. I'm buying the food tomorrow.

Hana: What a pity — I'm afraid I can't. I'm flying to Dublin on Saturday morning. My cousin is getting married.

Greta: Never mind, Hana. Another time! Have a lovely wedding.

Omar: Sounds great, but I might be late. I'm working until six, and then I'm picking up my son from football.

Greta: No problem, Omar. Bring him too.

Omar: Thanks! He'll be very happy. What about the weather? The forecast says it might rain.

Greta: I know. If it rains, we'll eat inside. I'll let you know on Saturday morning.

Luis: Shall we make a salad? Hana's recipe?

Hana: I'll send it to you right now.

tr.en: Summary: Greta invites her friends to a barbecue on Saturday at five in her garden to celebrate her new job. Luis would love to come and offers to bring something; Greta asks for drinks — she is buying the food tomorrow. Hana can't come: she is flying to Dublin on Saturday morning for her cousin's wedding. Omar might be late: he is working until six and then picking up his son from football; Greta says to bring him too. The forecast says it might rain; if it rains, they'll eat inside, and Greta will let them know on Saturday morning. Hana will send Luis her salad recipe.

text.ru: Часто с *I think, I'm sure, I hope, probably*: *I think it**'ll** be fine.* · *You**'ll probably** get the job.* Отрицательное мнение: ***I don't think** he**'ll** come.* — отрицание в английском ставят в *think*, а не во вторую часть. *probably* стоит после *will*, но перед *won't*: *She probably won't come.*

text.en: You decide **while you are speaking**: *The phone is ringing. — I**'ll** get it.* · *I**'ll have** the soup, please.* Compare a plan made before: *I**'m going to** have soup — I bought the vegetables yesterday.*
text.ru: Вы решаете **в момент речи**: *The phone is ringing. — I**'ll** get it.* · *I**'ll have** the soup, please.* (заказ в кафе). Сравните с заранее принятым планом: *I**'m going to** have soup — I bought the vegetables yesterday.*

text.en: For something **fixed** — with a time, a place or another person, often in your diary — use the **present continuous** + a future time: *I**'m seeing** the dentist **at ten tomorrow**.* · *We**'re having** people round **on Saturday**.*

text.en: ***What are you doing** this evening / on Friday / at the weekend?* — *Nothing special. I**'m staying in**.* · ***Are you doing** anything on Sunday?* — *Yes, I**'m meeting** Sam.*

text.en: Sorry + a reason (an arrangement!): ***I'm afraid I can't.** I**'m flying** to Dublin on Saturday.* · *I'd love to, **but** I'm working.* The host: ***What a pity! Never mind. Another time.***

text.en: *If it **rains**, we**'ll eat** inside.* · *I**'ll let you know** on Saturday morning.* After **if** — the present, not *will*. (More in Unit 9.)
text.ru: *If it **rains**, we**'ll eat** inside.* · *I**'ll let you know** on Saturday morning.* После **if** — настоящее время, а не *will*, хотя по-русски «если пойдёт». (Подробнее — в главе 9.)

flats.title: Two flats
flats.text:
Emre: So, which flat do you prefer — the one in Park Street or the one in Mill Lane?
Julia: It's difficult. The Park Street flat is bigger and much brighter. The living room has two windows.
Emre: And the view is better. You can see the river.
Julia: Yes, but it's more expensive. The rent is higher, and it's further from my office.
Emre: How much further?
Julia: About twenty minutes by bus. Mill Lane is more convenient: I can walk to work.
Emre: But Mill Lane is noisier. There's a bar downstairs.
Julia: True. And the kitchen is smaller and a bit darker.
Emre: Is the neighbourhood safe?
Julia: Both neighbourhoods are safe. Mill Lane is more crowded, but it's also livelier. There are more shops and cafés.
Emre: What about the landlords?
Julia: The Park Street landlord was friendlier. The one in Mill Lane was even later than me — and I was ten minutes late.
Emre: So Park Street is quieter, brighter and bigger, and Mill Lane is cheaper and closer.
Julia: Exactly. I think sleeping well is more important than walking to work. I'll take Park Street.

tr.en: Summary: Julia is choosing between two flats. The Park Street flat is bigger and much brighter, with a better view of the river, and its landlord was friendlier — but the rent is higher and it is about twenty minutes further from her office by bus. The Mill Lane flat is cheaper, closer (she can walk to work) and in a livelier, more crowded neighbourhood with more shops — but it is noisier (a bar downstairs), and the kitchen is smaller and a bit darker. Both neighbourhoods are safe. Julia decides that sleeping well is more important than walking to work and takes Park Street.

planet.title: Our planet
planet.text:
Here are some facts about our planet and its neighbours. How many do you know?

The highest mountain on Earth is Mount Everest, in the Himalayas. The largest and deepest ocean is the Pacific: it is bigger than all the land on Earth together.

The largest country in the world is Russia, and the smallest is Vatican City, which is inside the city of Rome.

The coldest continent is Antarctica. It is also the windiest and the driest — yes, drier than the deserts of Africa, because it almost never rains or snows there.

The largest animal on Earth is the blue whale. The fastest animal on land is the cheetah, but it is not the fastest animal of all: some birds are faster when they fly down from the sky.

And in space? The biggest planet near our Sun is Jupiter. The smallest is Mercury, which is also the closest to the Sun. But Mercury is not the hottest planet. Venus is further from the Sun, and it is even hotter.

tr.en: Summary: Facts in superlatives. The highest mountain is Everest; the largest and deepest ocean is the Pacific, bigger than all the land together. The largest country is Russia, the smallest Vatican City, inside Rome. Antarctica is the coldest, windiest and driest continent — drier than African deserts. The blue whale is the largest animal; the cheetah is the fastest on land, but some birds are faster when flying down. Jupiter is the biggest planet near our Sun; Mercury is the smallest and closest to the Sun, but Venus, though further away, is even hotter.
tr.ru:
Вот несколько фактов о нашей планете и её соседях. Сколько из них вы знаете?

Самая высокая гора на Земле — Эверест в Гималаях. Самый большой и самый глубокий океан — Тихий: он больше, чем вся суша Земли вместе взятая.

Самая большая страна в мире — Россия, а самая маленькая — Ватикан, который находится внутри Рима.

Самый холодный континент — Антарктида. Он же самый ветреный и самый сухой — да, суше африканских пустынь, потому что дождь и снег там почти не выпадают.

Самое крупное животное на Земле — синий кит. Самое быстрое животное на суше — гепард, но он не самый быстрый из всех: некоторые птицы летят быстрее, когда пикируют с неба.

А в космосе? Самая большая планета возле нашего Солнца — Юпитер. Самая маленькая — Меркурий, он же ближе всех к Солнцу. Но Меркурий — не самая горячая планета. Венера дальше от Солнца, и она ещё горячее.

review.title: Two cafés in my street
review.text:
There are two cafés in my street, and people often ask me which one is better. Here is my opinion.

The Corner Cup is the older one. It is small and dark, but the atmosphere is lovely, and the staff are the friendliest in town — they know my name and my order. The coffee is excellent. On the other hand, it is always crowded, the chairs are not very comfortable, and it is too noisy to work there.

Bean House opened last year. It is much more modern and more spacious, and it has the fastest wi-fi in the neighbourhood. It is quiet enough for work, and the cakes are better than at the Corner Cup. However, the coffee is not as good, and it is more expensive. The service is slower too, and one waiter was quite rude to me.

Overall, the Corner Cup is better value for money. In my opinion, it is the best place for a quick coffee with a friend. But if you need to work for a few hours, Bean House is worth the higher price. I recommend both — for different days.

tr.en: Summary: A review comparing two cafés. The Corner Cup is older, small and dark, with a lovely atmosphere, the friendliest staff in town and excellent coffee; but it is always crowded, the chairs are not very comfortable and it is too noisy to work there. Bean House, opened last year, is much more modern and spacious, has the fastest wi-fi in the neighbourhood, is quiet enough for work and has better cakes; but the coffee is not as good, it is more expensive, the service is slower and one waiter was rude. Overall the Corner Cup is better value for money and best for a quick coffee; Bean House is worth the price for working.
tr.ru:
На моей улице два кафе, и меня часто спрашивают, какое лучше. Вот моё мнение.

«Корнер Кап» — то, что постарше. Оно маленькое и тёмное, но атмосфера там чудесная, а персонал — самый приветливый в городе: там знают моё имя и мой заказ. Кофе превосходный. С другой стороны, там всегда полно народу, стулья не очень удобные, и для работы там слишком шумно.

«Бин Хаус» открылся в прошлом году. Он гораздо современнее и просторнее, и там самый быстрый вайфай в районе. Для работы там достаточно тихо, а пирожные лучше, чем в «Корнер Кап». Однако кофе не такой хороший, и стоит он дороже. Обслуживание тоже медленнее, а один официант был со мной довольно груб.

В целом «Корнер Кап» больше стоит своих денег. По-моему, это лучшее место, чтобы быстро выпить кофе с другом. Но если нужно поработать несколько часов, «Бин Хаус» оправдывает более высокую цену. Рекомендую оба — для разных дней.

text.en: One syllable → **-er**: *cheap → cheap**er***, *bright → bright**er***. Mind the spelling.
text.ru: Один слог → **-er**: *cheap → cheap**er***, *bright → bright**er***. Следите за правописанием.

text.en: Two or more syllables (not ending in -y) → **more**: ***more** expensive, **more** modern, **more** convenient*. The opposite is **less**: ***less** expensive*. Never both: not ~~more cheaper~~.
text.ru: Два слога и больше (не на -y) → **more**: ***more** expensive, **more** modern, **more** convenient*. Противоположное — **less**: ***less** expensive*. Не оба сразу: не ~~more cheaper~~, не ~~more better~~. По-русски «более дешёвый» и «дешевле» — оба возможны, в английском форма одна.

text.en: *good → **better*** · *bad → **worse*** · *far → **further***.
text.ru: *good → **better*** · *bad → **worse*** · *far → **further***.

text.en: *Mill Lane is noisier **than** Park Street.* · *She was later **than me**.* The word is **than**, not *that* or *then*.
text.ru: *Mill Lane is noisier **than** Park Street.* · *She was later **than me**.* Слово — **than** («чем»), не *that* и не *then*. После него в разговорной речи — *me, him, her*: *older than me*.

text.en: ***much / a lot** bigger* (big difference) · ***a bit / a little** bigger* (small difference) · ***even** bigger* (it was big, this one is more so). Not ~~very bigger~~.
text.ru: ***much / a lot** bigger* (намного) · ***a bit / a little** bigger* (немного) · ***even** bigger* (ещё больше). Не ~~very bigger~~: *very* со сравнительной степенью не употребляется.

text.en: Short: **the + -est** (same spelling rules as -er). Long: **the most** + adjective. Don't forget **the**.

text.en: **in** + a place or a group as one thing: *the highest mountain **in** the world*, *the best student **in** the class*. **of** + plural or a period: *the fastest **of** all*, *the best day **of** my life*.
text.ru: **in** + место или группа как целое: *the highest mountain **in** the world*, *the best student **in** the class*. **of** + множественное число или период: *the fastest **of** all*, *the best day **of** my life*. Русское «самый высокий в мире» — **in** the world, а не ~~of the world~~.
